findings.summary: In extract_rust, the calls-edge dict literal was updated to "confidence": "EXTRACTED" but the adjacent "weight" field was left at 0.8 instead of 1.0 (every other touched extractor — generic/Python, Go, Zig, PowerShell, Objective-C, Elixir — correctly pairs EXTRACTED with weight 1.0). This leaves Rust calls edges internally inconsistent (EXTRACTED confidence tag with an INFERRED-level weight), directly contradicting the brief's requirement that AST-resolved calls edges be tagged confidence="EXTRACTED" and weight=1.0. No test catches it because test_rust_calls_are_extracted (tests/test_multilang.py) only asserts on confidence, not weight — same as the pre-existing test, so the gap was never exercised.

findings.summary: The docstring for test_calls_edges_emitted still reads "Call-graph pass must produce INFERRED calls edges" even though the very next test in the same file was renamed/updated to assert EXTRACTED. Purely cosmetic (the test itself doesn't assert on confidence), but it's now an inaccurate statement sitting one line above the corrected test.
